contrast.wrong: You are coming to the party, isn't it?
contrast.right: You are coming to the party, aren't you?
contrast.why_en: The tag must match the subject and auxiliary: you are → aren't you. 'Isn't it' is the all-purpose Indian tag copied from Hindi 'है ना'.
contrast.why_hi: Tag में वही subject और auxiliary चाहिए: you are → aren't you। 'Isn't it' हिन्दी 'है ना' की नकल है।

contrast.wrong: He likes chai, no?
contrast.right: He likes chai, doesn't he?
contrast.why_en: 'No?' as a tag is Indian/European English; standard English builds the tag from the verb.
contrast.why_hi: 'No?' tag भारतीय/यूरोपीय अंग्रेज़ी है; मानक अंग्रेज़ी में tag verb से बनता है।

contrast.wrong: She has finished, hasn't it?
contrast.right: She has finished, hasn't she?
contrast.why_en: The pronoun must match the subject: she → she.
contrast.why_hi: Pronoun subject से मेल खाना चाहिए: she → she।

contrast.wrong: You didn't call him, didn't you?
contrast.right: You didn't call him, did you?
contrast.why_en: Negative statement → positive tag. Same polarity twice is wrong.
contrast.why_hi: Negative statement → positive tag। दोनों एक ही polarity में गलत है।

practice.prompt: You're the new analyst, ___ you?
practice.hi: आप नए विश्लेषक हैं, है ना?
practice.feedback_hi: you're → aren't you।

practice.prompt: She works in Hyderabad, isn't it?
answer: She works in Hyderabad, doesn't she?
practice.hi: वह हैदराबाद में काम करती है, है ना?
practice.feedback_en: No auxiliary → does; subject she → doesn't she.
practice.feedback_hi: Auxiliary नहीं → does; subject she → doesn't she।

practice.prompt: They haven't patched the server yet, ___?
practice.hi: उन्होंने अभी तक सर्वर पैच नहीं किया, है ना?
practice.feedback_en: Negative statement → positive tag with the same auxiliary.
practice.feedback_hi: Negative statement → वही auxiliary, positive tag।

practice.prompt: The call was at 3, ___ it?
practice.hi: कॉल 3 बजे थी, है ना?
practice.feedback_hi: was → wasn't it।

practice.prompt: 'I'm right, aren't I?' — Correct?
practice.hi: मैं सही हूँ, है ना?
practice.feedback_en: Yes — 'aren't I' is the standard tag for 'I am'.
practice.feedback_hi: हाँ — 'I am' का मानक tag 'aren't I' है।

practice.prompt: You can join tomorrow, no?
answer: You can join tomorrow, can't you?
practice.hi: आप कल जुड़ सकते हैं, है ना?
practice.feedback_hi: can → can't you।

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
answer: Let's begin the review, shall we?
practice.hi: चलो समीक्षा शुरू करें, ठीक?
practice.feedback_hi: Let's → shall we।

practice.prompt: Pass me the cable, ___?
practice.hi: केबल दे दो, ठीक?
practice.feedback_hi: आदेश → will you / would you।

practice.prompt: Nobody saw the alert, didn't they?
answer: Nobody saw the alert, did they?
practice.hi: किसी ने अलर्ट नहीं देखा, है ना?
practice.feedback_en: 'Nobody' is negative in meaning → positive tag 'did they'.
practice.feedback_hi: 'Nobody' अर्थ में negative है → positive tag 'did they'।

practice.prompt: It's a critical vulnerability, ___ it?
practice.hi: यह गंभीर कमज़ोरी है, है ना?
practice.feedback_en: Here 'isn't it' is correct — because the statement really is 'it is'.
practice.feedback_hi: यहाँ 'isn't it' सही है — क्योंकि statement सचमुच 'it is' है।

production.task_en: Write 3 statements with question tags you might say in a meeting: one positive → negative tag, one negative → positive tag, and one with 'have' or 'can'. No 'isn't it', 'no?' or 'na?'.
production.task_hi: मीटिंग में कहने लायक question tag वाले 3 वाक्य लिखें: एक positive → negative tag, एक negative → positive tag, और एक 'have' या 'can' के साथ। 'isn't it', 'no?' या 'na?' नहीं।

title: Third conditional and mixed conditionals
concept_en: The third conditional talks about an imaginary past: something did not happen, and we imagine a different past result. The 'if' part uses the past perfect (had + past participle) and the result part uses would have + past participle. A mixed conditional joins two times: a past condition with a present result (If I had studied, I would be a doctor now), or a present condition with a past result (If I were braver, I would have spoken up). Hindi speakers often use the simple past in the result clause ('I would got') or drop 'have'. Keep the full form: would have + past participle.
concept_hi: थर्ड कंडीशनल एक काल्पनिक अतीत की बात करता है: कुछ हुआ नहीं था, और हम सोचते हैं कि अगर हुआ होता तो नतीजा क्या होता। 'if' वाले हिस्से में past perfect (had + verb का तीसरा रूप) आता है और नतीजे वाले हिस्से में would have + तीसरा रूप। मिक्स्ड कंडीशनल दो समयों को जोड़ता है: अतीत की शर्त और वर्तमान का नतीजा (If I had studied, I would be a doctor now), या वर्तमान की शर्त और अतीत का नतीजा। हिंदी भाषी अक्सर 'would got' कह देते हैं या 'have' छोड़ देते हैं। पूरा रूप रखें: would have + तीसरा रूप।
pattern: Third: If + had + V3, would/could/might + have + V3 | Mixed (past→present): If + had + V3, would + V1 (now) | Mixed (present→past): If + past simple / were, would have + V3

examples.en: If we had patched the server, the attacker would not have got in.
examples.hi: अगर हमने सर्वर को पैच किया होता, तो हमलावर अंदर नहीं आ पाता।
examples.note: Third conditional: past condition, past result.

examples.en: If I had known about the meeting, I would have joined.
examples.hi: अगर मुझे मीटिंग के बारे में पता होता, तो मैं शामिल हो गया होता।

examples.en: She could have finished earlier if she had started on time.
examples.hi: अगर वह समय पर शुरू करती, तो वह पहले ख़त्म कर सकती थी।
examples.note: Result clause can come first. 'could have' = ability that did not happen.

examples.en: If the logs had been enabled, we might have found the cause.
examples.hi: अगर लॉग चालू होते, तो शायद हमें कारण मिल जाता।
examples.note: 'might have' shows a possible, not certain, result.

examples.en: If I had taken that job in Pune, I would be living there now.
examples.hi: अगर मैंने पुणे वाली नौकरी ली होती, तो मैं अब वहीं रह रहा होता।

examples.en: If he were more careful, he wouldn't have deleted the database.
examples.hi: अगर वह ज़्यादा सावधान होता, तो उसने डेटाबेस डिलीट नहीं किया होता।

examples.en: We wouldn't be in this mess if the vendor had disclosed the bug.
examples.hi: अगर वेंडर ने बग की जानकारी दी होती, तो हम इस मुसीबत में नहीं होते।

examples.en: Had we tested the update, the outage would never have happened.
examples.hi: अगर हमने अपडेट को टेस्ट किया होता, तो यह आउटेज कभी नहीं होता।

examples.en: If you hadn't reminded me, I would have forgotten the deadline.
examples.hi: अगर तुमने याद न दिलाया होता, तो मैं डेडलाइन भूल गया होता।

examples.en: If she weren't so busy, she would have replied to your email yesterday.
examples.hi: अगर वह इतनी व्यस्त न होती, तो उसने कल तुम्हारे ईमेल का जवाब दे दिया होता।

contrast.wrong: If I would have known, I would have come.
contrast.right: If I had known, I would have come.
contrast.why_en: Never put 'would' in the if-clause. The condition uses had + V3.
contrast.why_hi: 'if' वाले हिस्से में 'would' कभी नहीं आता। शर्त में had + तीसरा रूप आता है।

contrast.wrong: If we had fixed it, the system would not crashed.
contrast.right: If we had fixed it, the system would not have crashed.
contrast.why_en: The result needs 'have' + past participle. Hindi 'क्रैश नहीं होता' has no separate word for 'have', so it gets dropped.
contrast.why_hi: नतीजे में 'have' + तीसरा रूप ज़रूरी है। हिंदी में 'नहीं होता' में 'have' जैसा अलग शब्द नहीं है, इसलिए यह छूट जाता है।

contrast.wrong: If I had studied harder, I would have been a doctor now.
contrast.right: If I had studied harder, I would be a doctor now.
contrast.why_en: The result is about NOW, so use a mixed conditional with 'would be', not 'would have been'.
contrast.why_hi: नतीजा 'अब' का है, इसलिए मिक्स्ड कंडीशनल में 'would be' आएगा, 'would have been' नहीं।

contrast.wrong: If he had money, he would have bought the car last year.
contrast.right: If he had had money, he would have bought the car last year.
contrast.why_en: For a past condition you need 'had had'. It looks odd but it is correct: had (auxiliary) + had (past participle of have).
contrast.why_hi: अतीत की शर्त के लिए 'had had' चाहिए। अजीब लगता है पर सही है: पहला had सहायक क्रिया, दूसरा had तीसरा रूप।

practice.prompt: If they ___ (test) the code, the bug would not have reached production.
practice.hi: अगर उन्होंने कोड टेस्ट किया होता, तो बग प्रोडक्शन तक नहीं पहुँचता।
practice.feedback_en: Third conditional if-clause: had + past participle → 'had tested'.
practice.feedback_hi: थर्ड कंडीशनल के if वाले हिस्से में had + तीसरा रूप: 'had tested'।

practice.prompt: If I had seen the alert, I ___ the incident sooner.
practice.hi: अगर मैंने अलर्ट देखा होता, तो मैंने घटना की सूचना पहले दे दी होती।
practice.feedback_en: Past result → would have + past participle.
practice.feedback_hi: अतीत का नतीजा → would have + तीसरा रूप।

practice.prompt: If I would have left earlier, I would have caught the train.
answer: If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train.
practice.hi: अगर मैं पहले निकलता, तो मुझे ट्रेन मिल जाती।
practice.feedback_en: 'would' does not belong in the if-clause. Use 'had left'.
practice.feedback_hi: 'would' if वाले हिस्से में नहीं आता। 'had left' लिखें।

practice.prompt: If she had accepted the offer, she ___ in London now.
practice.hi: अगर उसने ऑफ़र स्वीकार किया होता, तो वह अब लंदन में रह रही होती।
practice.feedback_en: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result → 'would be living' (or 'would live').
practice.feedback_hi: मिक्स्ड कंडीशनल: अतीत की शर्त, वर्तमान नतीजा → 'would be living'।

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
answer: If we had known, we would have waited.
practice.hi: अगर हमें पता होता, तो हम इंतज़ार करते।
practice.feedback_en: If + had known, would have + waited.
practice.feedback_hi: If + had known, would have + waited।

practice.prompt: The breach would not happened if MFA had been enabled.
answer: The breach would not have happened if MFA had been enabled.
The breach wouldn't have happened if MFA had been enabled.
practice.hi: अगर MFA चालू होता, तो यह सेंधमारी नहीं होती।
practice.feedback_en: Result clause needs 'have': would not have happened.
practice.feedback_hi: नतीजे वाले हिस्से में 'have' चाहिए: would not have happened।

practice.prompt: 'If he weren't so lazy, he would have finished the report' is a correct mixed conditional.
practice.hi: 'अगर वह इतना आलसी न होता, तो उसने रिपोर्ट पूरी कर ली होती' — क्या यह सही मिक्स्ड कंडीशनल है?
practice.feedback_en: True. Present/general condition (weren't) + past result (would have finished).
practice.feedback_hi: सही। वर्तमान की शर्त (weren't) + अतीत का नतीजा (would have finished)।

practice.prompt: ___ we backed up the data, we could have restored it in minutes. (formal, no 'if')
practice.hi: अगर हमने डेटा का बैकअप लिया होता, तो हम मिनटों में उसे बहाल कर सकते थे।
practice.feedback_en: Formal inversion: 'Had we backed up' = 'If we had backed up'.
practice.feedback_hi: औपचारिक रूप: 'Had we backed up' = 'If we had backed up'।

practice.prompt: If the developer ___ more experience, he wouldn't have written that query.
practice.hi: अगर डेवलपर के पास ज़्यादा अनुभव होता, तो वह वैसी क्वेरी न लिखता।
practice.feedback_en: Mixed: a present/general fact (he still lacks experience) → past simple 'had' in the if-clause. 'Had had' would mean he lacked it only at that past moment.
practice.feedback_hi: मिक्स्ड: यह अब भी सच है (अनुभव कम है), इसलिए if में past simple 'had'। 'had had' का मतलब होता कि सिर्फ़ उस समय अनुभव कम था।

practice.prompt: If you had told me, I would help you.
answer: If you had told me, I would have helped you.
practice.hi: अगर तुमने मुझे बताया होता, तो मैं तुम्हारी मदद करता।
practice.feedback_en: The help was needed in the past, so the result must be 'would have helped'.
practice.feedback_hi: मदद अतीत में चाहिए थी, इसलिए नतीजा 'would have helped' होगा।

production.task_en: Write 3 sentences about a real mistake at work or in study: one third conditional, one mixed conditional (past→present), and one formal 'Had I…' sentence.
production.task_hi: काम या पढ़ाई की किसी असली गलती के बारे में 3 वाक्य लिखें: एक थर्ड कंडीशनल, एक मिक्स्ड (अतीत→वर्तमान), और एक औपचारिक 'Had I…' वाक्य।

title: Wish / if only / would rather / it's time
concept_en: 'Wish' and 'if only' express regret or a desire for things to be different. For the present, use wish + past simple (I wish I knew). For the past, use wish + past perfect (I wish I had known). For an annoying habit or something you want to change, use wish + would (I wish he would stop). 'Would rather' + bare verb states a preference (I'd rather stay); with a different subject it takes the past simple (I'd rather you stayed). 'It's time' + past simple means something should already be happening (It's time we left). Hindi speakers often say 'I wish I know' or 'I wish to…' when they mean regret.
concept_hi: 'Wish' और 'if only' पछतावा या यह इच्छा जताते हैं कि चीज़ें अलग होतीं। वर्तमान के लिए wish + past simple (I wish I knew)। अतीत के लिए wish + past perfect (I wish I had known)। किसी की परेशान करने वाली आदत के लिए wish + would (I wish he would stop)। 'Would rather' + क्रिया का पहला रूप पसंद बताता है (I'd rather stay); दूसरा कर्ता हो तो past simple (I'd rather you stayed)। 'It's time' + past simple का मतलब है कि यह काम अब तक हो जाना चाहिए था (It's time we left)। हिंदी भाषी अक्सर 'I wish I know' कह देते हैं।
pattern: wish/if only + past simple (present regret) | wish/if only + past perfect (past regret) | wish + would (annoyance/change) | would rather + V1 / would rather + subject + past simple | it's (high) time + past simple

examples.en: I wish I spoke English more fluently.
examples.hi: काश मैं अंग्रेज़ी ज़्यादा धाराप्रवाह बोल पाता।

examples.en: If only we had kept a backup.
examples.hi: काश हमने बैकअप रखा होता।

examples.en: I wish my manager would reply to emails faster.
examples.hi: काश मेरा मैनेजर ईमेल का जवाब जल्दी देता।
examples.note: wish + would: wanting someone's behaviour to change.

examples.en: She wishes she were taller.
examples.hi: वह चाहती है कि वह लंबी होती।
examples.note: 'were' is used for all persons after wish in formal English.

examples.en: I'd rather work from home on Fridays.
examples.hi: मैं शुक्रवार को घर से काम करना ज़्यादा पसंद करूँगा।

examples.en: I'd rather you didn't share that report outside the team.
examples.hi: मैं चाहूँगा कि आप वह रिपोर्ट टीम के बाहर साझा न करें।

examples.en: It's time we upgraded the firewall.
examples.hi: अब समय आ गया है कि हम फ़ायरवॉल अपग्रेड करें।
examples.note: it's time + past simple = should already be done.

examples.en: If only I hadn't clicked that link!
examples.hi: काश मैंने उस लिंक पर क्लिक न किया होता!

examples.en: I wish it would stop raining.
examples.hi: काश बारिश रुक जाती।
examples.note: wish + would for a situation you want to change.

examples.en: He would rather have stayed in Ahmedabad than moved to Bangalore.
examples.hi: वह बेंगलुरु जाने के बजाय अहमदाबाद में ही रहना पसंद करता।
examples.note: Past preference: would rather have + V3.

contrast.wrong: I wish I know the answer.
contrast.right: I wish I knew the answer.
contrast.why_en: A present wish takes the past simple. Hindi 'काश मुझे पता होता' uses a special mood; English shows it with a past form.
contrast.why_hi: वर्तमान की इच्छा में past simple आता है। हिंदी 'काश … होता' में अलग रूप है; अंग्रेज़ी इसे past रूप से दिखाती है।

contrast.wrong: I wish I would have studied harder.
contrast.right: I wish I had studied harder.
contrast.why_en: For past regret use past perfect, never 'would have' after wish.
contrast.why_hi: अतीत के पछतावे में past perfect आता है, wish के बाद 'would have' नहीं।

contrast.wrong: I would rather to go home.
contrast.right: I would rather go home.
contrast.why_en: 'Would rather' is followed by the bare infinitive, no 'to'.
contrast.why_hi: 'Would rather' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता, सीधे क्रिया आती है।

contrast.wrong: It's time to we leave.
contrast.right: It's time we left. / It's time to leave.
contrast.why_en: Either 'it's time + to-infinitive' or 'it's time + subject + past simple'. Do not mix them.
contrast.why_hi: या तो 'it's time + to + क्रिया' या 'it's time + कर्ता + past simple'। दोनों को मिलाएँ नहीं।

practice.prompt: I wish I ___ (have) more time to practise speaking.
practice.hi: काश मेरे पास बोलने का अभ्यास करने के लिए ज़्यादा समय होता।
practice.feedback_hi: वर्तमान की इच्छा → past simple 'had'।

practice.prompt: If only we ___ (read) the documentation before deploying.
practice.hi: काश हमने डिप्लॉय करने से पहले डॉक्युमेंटेशन पढ़ा होता।
practice.feedback_hi: अतीत का पछतावा → past perfect 'had read'।

practice.prompt: I wish my neighbour ___ playing loud music at night.
practice.hi: काश मेरा पड़ोसी रात में तेज़ संगीत बजाना बंद कर देता।
practice.feedback_en: Annoying habit you want changed → wish + would.
practice.feedback_hi: परेशान करने वाली आदत बदलवाने के लिए → wish + would।

practice.prompt: I would rather to stay at home tonight.
answer: I would rather stay at home tonight.
I'd rather stay at home tonight.
practice.hi: मैं आज रात घर पर रहना ज़्यादा पसंद करूँगा।
practice.feedback_hi: 'would rather' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता।

practice.prompt: I'd rather you ___ the client directly; go through me first.
practice.hi: मैं चाहूँगा कि आप क्लाइंट से सीधे संपर्क न करें; पहले मुझसे बात करें।
practice.feedback_en: Would rather + different subject → past simple.
practice.feedback_hi: would rather + दूसरा कर्ता → past simple।

practice.prompt: It's high time the company invests in training.
answer: It's high time the company invested in training.
practice.hi: अब बहुत समय हो गया है कि कंपनी प्रशिक्षण में निवेश करे।
practice.feedback_hi: 'It's (high) time' + past simple: 'invested'।

production.task_en: Write 3 sentences: one 'I wish' about your English now, one 'if only' about something in the past, and one 'I'd rather' about how you prefer to work.

title: Passive: advanced (modals, get-passive, 'it is said that')
concept_en: You already know be + past participle. At B2 you need the passive with modals (must be reviewed, should have been fixed), the get-passive for informal or unexpected events (he got fired, the site got hacked), and reporting passives used in news and reports: 'It is said that he left' or 'He is said to have left'. Reporting passives let you present claims without naming the source, which is exactly the tone of a security report ('The vulnerability is believed to be exploited in the wild'). Watch the tense of the infinitive: 'is believed to be' (now) versus 'is believed to have been' (earlier).
concept_hi: आप be + तीसरा रूप जानते हैं। B2 पर modals के साथ passive चाहिए (must be reviewed, should have been fixed), अनौपचारिक या अचानक घटनाओं के लिए get-passive (he got fired, the site got hacked), और रिपोर्टिंग passive जो ख़बरों और रिपोर्ट में आता है: 'It is said that he left' या 'He is said to have left'। रिपोर्टिंग passive से आप स्रोत का नाम लिए बिना दावा रख सकते हैं — सिक्योरिटी रिपोर्ट का यही लहजा है। infinitive का काल ध्यान रखें: 'is believed to be' (अभी) बनाम 'is believed to have been' (पहले)।
pattern: modal + be + V3 | modal + have been + V3 | get + V3 | It is said/believed/reported that + clause | Subject + is said/believed + to + V1 / to have + V3

examples.en: All pull requests must be reviewed before merging.

examples.en: Our website got defaced over the weekend.
examples.hi: सप्ताहांत में हमारी वेबसाइट को विकृत कर दिया गया।

examples.hi: ऑडिट के बाद उसे प्रमोशन मिल गया।

examples.en: The attackers are believed to have used stolen credentials.
examples.hi: माना जाता है कि हमलावरों ने चुराए गए क्रेडेंशियल इस्तेमाल किए थे।
examples.note: Same meaning; subject + is believed + to have + V3 (earlier action).

examples.en: The CEO is said to be considering a merger.
examples.hi: कहा जाता है कि सीईओ विलय पर विचार कर रहे हैं।

examples.hi: यह समस्या स्टेजिंग सर्वर पर दोहराई नहीं जा सकती।

examples.hi: किसी को यह पसंद नहीं कि उसे बताया जाए कि क्या करना है।

contrast.wrong: The report must reviewed by Friday.
contrast.right: The report must be reviewed by Friday.
contrast.why_en: After a modal you still need 'be' before the past participle.
contrast.why_hi: modal के बाद भी तीसरे रूप से पहले 'be' चाहिए।

contrast.wrong: It is said that he is left the company.
contrast.right: It is said that he has left the company. / He is said to have left the company.
contrast.why_en: Inside the that-clause use normal tenses; with the to-form use 'to have + V3' for a past action.
contrast.why_hi: that वाले हिस्से में सामान्य काल रखें; to वाले रूप में अतीत के लिए 'to have + तीसरा रूप'।

contrast.wrong: The server was got hacked.
contrast.right: The server got hacked. / The server was hacked.
contrast.why_en: Use either 'was' or 'got', never both.
contrast.why_hi: या तो 'was' या 'got', दोनों एक साथ नहीं।

contrast.wrong: The bug should be fixed yesterday.
contrast.right: The bug should have been fixed yesterday.
contrast.why_en: A past obligation that was not met needs 'should have been'. Hindi 'कल ठीक होना चाहिए था' maps to 'have been', not 'be'.
contrast.why_hi: अतीत की पूरी न हुई ज़िम्मेदारी के लिए 'should have been' चाहिए। हिंदी 'ठीक होना चाहिए था' = 'have been'।

practice.hi: पासवर्ड को salted hash के रूप में स्टोर किया जाना चाहिए।

practice.prompt: The certificate ___ before it expired, but nobody noticed.
practice.hi: सर्टिफ़िकेट के एक्सपायर होने से पहले उसे रिन्यू किया जाना चाहिए था, पर किसी ने ध्यान नहीं दिया।
practice.feedback_en: Past, not done → should have been + V3.
practice.feedback_hi: अतीत में नहीं हुआ → should have been + तीसरा रूप।

practice.prompt: It is thought that the malware is installed last month.
answer: It is thought that the malware was installed last month.

practice.feedback_en: 'Last month' → past simple inside the that-clause.
practice.feedback_hi: 'last month' → that वाले हिस्से में past simple।

practice.prompt: Rewrite: 'People say that the company is hiring.' → 'The company ___ hiring.'
practice.hi: कहा जाता है कि कंपनी भर्ती कर रही है।
practice.feedback_en: Present action → is said + to be + -ing.
practice.feedback_hi: वर्तमान क्रिया → is said + to be + -ing।

practice.prompt: Two employees ___ (get / fire) for sharing credentials.
practice.hi: क्रेडेंशियल साझा करने के लिए दो कर्मचारियों को निकाल दिया गया।
practice.feedback_hi: get-passive: got + तीसरा रूप।

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
answer: The attacker is believed to have gained access in March.
practice.hi: माना जाता है कि हमलावर ने मार्च में पहुँच हासिल की थी।
practice.feedback_en: Subject + is believed + to have + V3.
practice.feedback_hi: कर्ता + is believed + to have + तीसरा रूप।

practice.hi: 'नेटवर्क पर कोई भी डेटा तक पहुँच सकता है' — क्या यह modal passive सही है?
practice.feedback_hi: सही: can + be + accessed।

practice.prompt: The exploit is reported to be used in attacks last year.
answer: The exploit is reported to have been used in attacks last year.
practice.hi: रिपोर्ट के अनुसार यह एक्सप्लॉइट पिछले साल हमलों में इस्तेमाल हुआ था।
practice.feedback_en: Earlier action in passive → to have been + V3.
practice.feedback_hi: पहले हुई क्रिया passive में → to have been + तीसरा रूप।

practice.hi: मुझे प्रेज़ेंटेशन के दौरान टोका जाना पसंद नहीं।
practice.feedback_en: After 'hate' use the passive gerund: being + V3.
practice.feedback_hi: 'hate' के बाद passive gerund: being + तीसरा रूप।

practice.prompt: The issue might been caused by a race condition.
answer: The issue might have been caused by a race condition.
practice.hi: यह समस्या शायद रेस कंडीशन की वजह से हुई हो।
practice.feedback_en: might + have been + V3 for a past possibility.
practice.feedback_hi: अतीत की संभावना: might + have been + तीसरा रूप।

production.task_en: Write 3 sentences from a security report using passives: one with a modal (must/should be), one with 'is believed/reported to have', and one get-passive describing what happened to a system.
production.task_hi: सिक्योरिटी रिपोर्ट के 3 passive वाक्य लिखें: एक modal के साथ (must/should be), एक 'is believed/reported to have' के साथ, और एक get-passive जो बताए कि सिस्टम के साथ क्या हुआ।

title: Reported speech: questions, commands, reporting verbs
concept_en: To report a question, use normal statement word order and no question mark: 'Where is the file?' becomes 'She asked where the file was'. Yes/no questions need 'if' or 'whether'. Commands and requests use tell/ask + object + to-infinitive: 'Please restart it' becomes 'He asked me to restart it'. Beyond say and tell, use reporting verbs that carry meaning: suggest + -ing or that-clause, advise/warn/remind someone to do, deny/admit + -ing, promise/refuse/offer + to-infinitive. Hindi speakers often keep the question word order ('asked where was the file') and use 'told to me'.
concept_hi: सवाल रिपोर्ट करते समय सामान्य वाक्य-क्रम रखें और प्रश्नचिह्न न लगाएँ: 'Where is the file?' बन जाता है 'She asked where the file was'। हाँ/ना वाले सवालों में 'if' या 'whether' लगता है। आदेश और अनुरोध में tell/ask + व्यक्ति + to + क्रिया: 'Please restart it' → 'He asked me to restart it'। say और tell के अलावा अर्थ वाले reporting verbs इस्तेमाल करें: suggest + -ing या that, advise/warn/remind someone to do, deny/admit + -ing, promise/refuse/offer + to। हिंदी भाषी अक्सर सवाल का क्रम रख लेते हैं ('asked where was the file') और 'told to me' कहते हैं।
pattern: asked + wh-word + subject + verb | asked if/whether + subject + verb | told/asked + object + (not) to + V1 | suggested + -ing / that… | denied/admitted + -ing | promised/refused/offered + to + V1 | warned/reminded/advised + object + to + V1

examples.en: 'Where did you find the log?' → He asked me where I had found the log.
examples.hi: उसने मुझसे पूछा कि मुझे लॉग कहाँ मिला था।

examples.en: 'Is the server online?' → She asked whether the server was online.
examples.hi: उसने पूछा कि क्या सर्वर ऑनलाइन है।

examples.en: 'Don't touch production.' → The lead told us not to touch production.
examples.hi: लीड ने हमसे कहा कि प्रोडक्शन को न छुएँ।

examples.en: 'Could you send the report?' → He asked me to send the report.
examples.hi: उसने मुझसे रिपोर्ट भेजने को कहा।

examples.en: 'Let's rotate the keys.' → She suggested rotating the keys.
examples.hi: उसने चाबियाँ (keys) बदलने का सुझाव दिया।

examples.en: 'I didn't open the attachment.' → He denied opening the attachment.
examples.hi: उसने अटैचमेंट खोलने से इनकार किया।

examples.en: 'I'll fix it tonight.' → She promised to fix it tonight.
examples.hi: उसने आज रात ठीक करने का वादा किया।

examples.en: 'Remember to enable MFA.' → The admin reminded everyone to enable MFA.
examples.hi: एडमिन ने सबको MFA चालू करने की याद दिलाई।

examples.en: 'Don't use that library; it's abandoned.' → He warned me not to use that library.
examples.hi: उसने मुझे उस लाइब्रेरी का इस्तेमाल न करने की चेतावनी दी।

examples.en: 'Yes, I made the change.' → He admitted that he had made the change.
examples.hi: उसने माना कि उसने बदलाव किया था।

contrast.wrong: He asked me where was the file.
contrast.right: He asked me where the file was.
contrast.why_en: Reported questions use statement order (subject before verb). Hindi keeps the same order in direct and indirect, so learners copy the question form.
contrast.why_hi: रिपोर्टेड सवाल में वाक्य-क्रम सामान्य होता है (कर्ता पहले, क्रिया बाद)। हिंदी में प्रत्यक्ष और अप्रत्यक्ष का क्रम एक जैसा रहता है, इसलिए यह गलती होती है।

contrast.wrong: She told to me that the build failed.
contrast.right: She told me that the build failed. / She said to me that the build failed.
contrast.why_en: 'Tell' takes a direct object with no 'to'. 'Say' needs 'to'. Hindi 'मुझसे कहा' has a postposition, which becomes an extra 'to'.
contrast.why_hi: 'tell' के बाद सीधे व्यक्ति आता है, 'to' नहीं। 'say' के साथ 'to' चाहिए। हिंदी 'मुझसे कहा' का 'से' ग़लती से 'to' बन जाता है।

contrast.wrong: He suggested me to restart the service.
contrast.right: He suggested that I restart the service. / He suggested restarting the service.
contrast.why_en: 'Suggest' never takes object + to-infinitive.
contrast.why_hi: 'suggest' के बाद व्यक्ति + to + क्रिया कभी नहीं आता।

contrast.wrong: She asked that was I busy.
contrast.right: She asked if I was busy.
contrast.why_en: Yes/no questions are reported with if/whether and statement order.
contrast.why_hi: हाँ/ना वाले सवाल if/whether के साथ और सामान्य क्रम में रिपोर्ट होते हैं।

answer: The auditor asked me when I had last rotated the keys.
The auditor asked me when I last rotated the keys.
practice.hi: ऑडिटर ने मुझसे पूछा कि मैंने आखिरी बार keys कब बदली थीं।
practice.feedback_en: No 'did' and no question order in reported questions.
practice.feedback_hi: रिपोर्टेड सवाल में 'did' और सवाल वाला क्रम नहीं आता।

practice.prompt: 'Is the patch ready?' → She asked ___ the patch was ready.
practice.hi: उसने पूछा कि क्या पैच तैयार है।
practice.feedback_hi: हाँ/ना सवाल → whether/if।

practice.prompt: 'Please don't share the password.' → He asked us ___ (not / share) the password.
practice.hi: उसने हमसे पासवर्ड साझा न करने को कहा।
practice.feedback_en: Negative request → asked + object + not to + V1.
practice.feedback_hi: नकारात्मक अनुरोध → asked + व्यक्ति + not to + क्रिया।

practice.prompt: 'Why don't we add rate limiting?' → He suggested ___ rate limiting.
practice.hi: उसने रेट लिमिटिंग जोड़ने का सुझाव दिया।
practice.feedback_hi: suggest + -ing।

practice.prompt: She told to the team that the release was delayed.
answer: She told the team that the release was delayed.
practice.hi: उसने टीम को बताया कि रिलीज़ में देरी हो गई है।
practice.feedback_hi: tell + व्यक्ति, 'to' नहीं।

practice.prompt: 'I never accessed that folder.' → He denied ___ (access) that folder.
practice.hi: उसने उस फ़ोल्डर तक पहुँचने से इनकार किया।
practice.feedback_hi: deny + -ing।

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
answer: She reminded me to check the backups.
practice.hi: उसने मुझे बैकअप जाँचने की याद दिलाई।
practice.feedback_hi: remind + व्यक्ति + to + क्रिया।

practice.prompt: 'He refused to signing the contract' is correct.
practice.hi: 'He refused to signing the contract' सही है?
practice.feedback_en: False. refuse + to + V1: 'refused to sign'.
practice.feedback_hi: गलत। refuse + to + क्रिया: 'refused to sign'।

practice.prompt: 'You should update your browser.' → The IT desk ___ me to update my browser.
practice.hi: IT डेस्क ने मुझे ब्राउज़र अपडेट करने की सलाह दी।
practice.feedback_en: advise + object + to + V1. 'Said' and 'suggested' don't take this pattern.
practice.feedback_hi: advise + व्यक्ति + to + क्रिया। 'said' और 'suggested' इस पैटर्न में नहीं आते।

practice.prompt: The customer asked that how long would the fix take.
answer: The customer asked how long the fix would take.
practice.hi: ग्राहक ने पूछा कि फ़िक्स में कितना समय लगेगा।
practice.feedback_hi: 'that' हटाएँ; wh-सवाल + सामान्य क्रम।

production.task_en: Think of a real conversation from work this week. Report 3 things from it: one question someone asked, one request or instruction, and one thing using suggest/deny/promise/warn.
production.task_hi: इस हफ़्ते की एक असली बातचीत याद करें। उसकी 3 बातें रिपोर्ट करें: एक सवाल, एक अनुरोध या निर्देश, और एक वाक्य suggest/deny/promise/warn के साथ।

title: Relative clauses: non-defining, whose, where/when, prepositions
concept_en: A defining relative clause tells you which one (The engineer who wrote this left). A non-defining clause adds extra information and is separated by commas (Priya, who wrote this, has left). In non-defining clauses you cannot use 'that' and you cannot leave out the pronoun. 'Whose' shows possession for people and things (a company whose data was leaked). 'Where' replaces 'in which' for places, 'when' for times. A preposition can go at the end in speech (the team I work with) or before 'which/whom' in formal writing (the team with which I work). A relative clause can also comment on a whole sentence: 'The fix took two days, which surprised everyone.'
concept_hi: Defining relative clause बताता है कि कौन-सा (The engineer who wrote this left)। Non-defining clause अतिरिक्त जानकारी देता है और कॉमा से अलग होता है (Priya, who wrote this, has left)। Non-defining में 'that' नहीं आता और सर्वनाम छोड़ा नहीं जा सकता। 'Whose' लोगों और चीज़ों के स्वामित्व के लिए (a company whose data was leaked)। जगह के लिए 'where' (= in which), समय के लिए 'when'। बोलचाल में preposition अंत में (the team I work with), औपचारिक लेखन में which/whom से पहले (the team with which I work)। Relative clause पूरे वाक्य पर टिप्पणी भी कर सकता है: 'The fix took two days, which surprised everyone.'
pattern: Defining: noun + who/which/that (+ clause) | Non-defining: noun, + who/which (+ clause), | whose + noun | where = in/at which | when = on/at which | prep + which/whom (formal) | …, which + comment on whole clause

examples.en: Our CTO, who joined last year, used to work at a bank.

contrast.wrong: My brother, that lives in Surat, is a doctor.
contrast.right: My brother, who lives in Surat, is a doctor.
contrast.why_en: 'That' cannot introduce a non-defining clause (one with commas).

contrast.wrong: The company which its data was leaked apologised.
contrast.right: The company whose data was leaked apologised.
contrast.why_en: Possession needs 'whose', not 'which + its'. Hindi 'जिसका' is one word; 'whose' is its match.
contrast.why_hi: स्वामित्व के लिए 'whose' चाहिए, 'which + its' नहीं। हिंदी 'जिसका' = 'whose'।

contrast.wrong: This is the office where I work in.

contrast.why_en: 'Where' already includes the preposition. Use where OR a preposition, not both.

contrast.wrong: The manager who I reported to him left.
contrast.right: The manager I reported to left. / The manager to whom I reported left.
contrast.why_en: Do not repeat the object as a pronoun ('him'). Hindi allows 'जिसको … उसको', English does not.

practice.feedback_hi: सही। Defining clause में कर्म सर्वनाम हटाया जा सकता है: 'The laptop I bought'।

title: Phrasal verbs: separable vs inseparable
concept_en: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a particle (turn off, look after, put up with). With separable phrasal verbs the object can go after the particle or between the verb and the particle: 'turn off the light' or 'turn the light off'. But if the object is a pronoun (it, them, him), it MUST go in the middle: 'turn it off', never 'turn off it'. Inseparable phrasal verbs keep verb and particle together: 'look after the kids', 'look after them'. Three-part phrasal verbs (put up with, look forward to, get away with) are always inseparable. Hindi speakers most often make the pronoun mistake, because Hindi puts the object before the verb anyway and has no particle to split.
concept_hi: Phrasal verb = क्रिया + particle (turn off, look after, put up with)। Separable phrasal verb में कर्म particle के बाद या बीच में आ सकता है: 'turn off the light' या 'turn the light off'। लेकिन कर्म सर्वनाम हो (it, them, him) तो वह बीच में ही आएगा: 'turn it off', कभी 'turn off it' नहीं। Inseparable phrasal verb में क्रिया और particle साथ रहते हैं: 'look after the kids', 'look after them'। तीन हिस्सों वाले (put up with, look forward to, get away with) हमेशा inseparable होते हैं। हिंदी भाषी सबसे ज़्यादा सर्वनाम वाली गलती करते हैं, क्योंकि हिंदी में कर्म वैसे भी क्रिया से पहले आता है और तोड़ने के लिए particle नहीं होता।
pattern: Separable: V + noun + P / V + P + noun / V + PRONOUN + P | Inseparable: V + P + noun / V + P + pronoun | Three-part: V + P + P + object (never split)

contrast.wrong: I will pick up you at six.

title: Articles: advanced uses
concept_en: At this level the hard cases are: no article with abstract or general uncountable nouns (Security is everyone's job), but 'the' when the noun is made specific (The security of this system is poor). Institutions used for their purpose take no article (go to hospital, be in prison, at university), but the building itself takes 'the' (the hospital near my house). 'The' goes with superlatives, ordinals and 'only' (the best, the first, the only). Geography: 'the' with rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges, deserts and plural countries (the Ganges, the Himalayas, the Netherlands, the UAE), no article with single lakes, mountains, cities and most countries (Lake Pichola, Mount Everest, India). Jobs and nationalities in general take 'the' + adjective (the rich, the unemployed, the British).
concept_hi: इस स्तर पर कठिन मामले ये हैं: सामान्य/अमूर्त uncountable संज्ञा के साथ article नहीं (Security is everyone's job), लेकिन संज्ञा विशिष्ट हो तो 'the' (The security of this system is poor)। संस्था उसके उद्देश्य के लिए हो तो article नहीं (go to hospital, at university), लेकिन इमारत हो तो 'the' (the hospital near my house)। superlative, ordinal और 'only' के साथ 'the' (the best, the first, the only)। भूगोल: नदी, समुद्र, महासागर, पर्वतमाला, रेगिस्तान और बहुवचन देशों के साथ 'the' (the Ganges, the Himalayas, the Netherlands, the UAE); एक झील, एक पहाड़, शहर और ज़्यादातर देशों के साथ नहीं (Lake Pichola, Mount Everest, India)। समूह के लिए 'the' + विशेषण (the rich, the unemployed, the British)।
pattern: Ø + abstract/general uncountable | the + noun + of… (specific) | Ø + hospital/school/prison/university (purpose) vs the + building | the + superlative/ordinal/only | the + rivers/seas/ranges/plural countries | Ø + lakes/mountains/cities/most countries | the + adjective = group

examples.en: Knowledge is power.
examples.hi: ज्ञान ही शक्ति है।

examples.en: The knowledge we gained from the incident was priceless.
examples.hi: उस घटना से हमने जो सीखा, वह अनमोल था।
examples.note: Specific (we gained… from the incident) → the.

examples.en: My father is in hospital; I'm going to the hospital at six.
examples.hi: मेरे पिता अस्पताल में भर्ती हैं; मैं छह बजे अस्पताल जा रहा हूँ।

examples.en: She started university at seventeen.
examples.hi: उसने सत्रह की उम्र में यूनिवर्सिटी शुरू की।

examples.hi: यही एकमात्र सर्वर है जो अब भी Windows 2008 चलाता है।

examples.en: The Ganges flows through Varanasi.
examples.hi: गंगा वाराणसी से होकर बहती है।

examples.en: We trekked in the Himalayas and camped near Lake Tsomgo.
examples.hi: हमने हिमालय में ट्रेकिंग की और त्सोमगो झील के पास कैंप किया।
examples.note: Range → the; single lake → no article.

examples.en: She moved from India to the Netherlands last year.
examples.hi: वह पिछले साल भारत से नीदरलैंड चली गई।

examples.en: The government should do more for the unemployed.
examples.hi: सरकार को बेरोज़गारों के लिए और करना चाहिए।

examples.en: It was the third breach this year, and the worst by far.
examples.hi: यह इस साल की तीसरी सेंधमारी थी, और अब तक की सबसे बुरी।

contrast.wrong: The security is important for every company.
contrast.right: Security is important for every company.
contrast.why_en: General abstract noun → no article. Hindi speakers add 'the' to sound formal.
contrast.why_hi: सामान्य अमूर्त संज्ञा → article नहीं। औपचारिक दिखने के लिए हिंदी भाषी 'the' जोड़ देते हैं।

contrast.wrong: He is in the prison for fraud.
contrast.right: He is in prison for fraud.
contrast.why_en: In prison = as a prisoner (purpose). 'The prison' would just mean the building.
contrast.why_hi: in prison = कैदी के रूप में (उद्देश्य)। 'the prison' का मतलब सिर्फ़ इमारत होगा।

contrast.wrong: I visited Himalayas and Ganges river.
contrast.right: I visited the Himalayas and the Ganges.
contrast.why_en: Mountain ranges and rivers take 'the'. Hindi has no article, so these fixed uses must be memorised.
contrast.why_hi: पर्वतमाला और नदी के साथ 'the' आता है। हिंदी में article नहीं है, इसलिए ये तय प्रयोग याद करने होंगे।

contrast.wrong: It is best solution we have.
contrast.right: It is the best solution we have.
contrast.why_en: Superlatives always take 'the'.
contrast.why_hi: Superlative के साथ हमेशा 'the'।

practice.prompt: ___ privacy is a fundamental right.

practice.feedback_hi: 'of our users' से विशिष्ट हुआ → the।

practice.prompt: My sister is studying at the university in Baroda.
answer: My sister is studying at university in Baroda.
My sister is studying at a university in Baroda.
practice.hi: मेरी बहन बड़ौदा में यूनिवर्सिटी में पढ़ रही है।
practice.feedback_en: As a student (purpose) → 'at university'. ('At a university' is also fine if you mean one of several.)
practice.feedback_hi: छात्र के रूप में (उद्देश्य) → 'at university'।

practice.prompt: This is ___ first time we've seen this malware family.
practice.hi: हमने यह मैलवेयर परिवार पहली बार देखा है।
practice.feedback_hi: Ordinal → the।

practice.prompt: They sailed across ___ Arabian Sea to ___ Oman.
practice.hi: वे अरब सागर पार करके ओमान गए।
practice.feedback_en: Seas take 'the'; most countries take no article.
practice.feedback_hi: समुद्र के साथ 'the'; ज़्यादातर देशों के साथ article नहीं।

title: Future perfect and future continuous
concept_en: The future continuous (will be + -ing) describes an action in progress at a point in the future: 'At 10 tomorrow I'll be presenting'. It is also a polite, neutral way to ask about plans: 'Will you be joining the call?'. The future perfect (will have + past participle) says an action will be complete before a future point: 'By Friday we will have migrated all users'. Both usually come with a time marker: 'at this time tomorrow', 'by next week', 'by the time'. Hindi speakers often use the simple future for both ('I will finish by Friday' is fine, but 'By Friday I will finish for two weeks' is wrong).
concept_hi: Future continuous (will be + -ing) भविष्य के किसी क्षण पर चल रही क्रिया बताता है: 'At 10 tomorrow I'll be presenting'। यह योजनाओं के बारे में पूछने का विनम्र तरीका भी है: 'Will you be joining the call?'। Future perfect (will have + तीसरा रूप) कहता है कि क्रिया भविष्य के किसी बिंदु से पहले पूरी हो जाएगी: 'By Friday we will have migrated all users'। दोनों के साथ अक्सर समय-सूचक आता है: 'at this time tomorrow', 'by next week', 'by the time'। हिंदी भाषी अक्सर दोनों के लिए simple future इस्तेमाल करते हैं।
pattern: will be + V-ing (in progress at a future time) | will have + V3 (complete by a future time) | will have been + V-ing (duration up to a future time) | by + time / by the time + clause / at this time + tomorrow

title: Used to / would / be used to / get used to
concept_en: These look alike but mean different things. 'Used to + verb' describes a past habit or state that is no longer true (I used to smoke). 'Would + verb' also describes repeated past actions, but only actions, not states (We would play cricket every evening, but NOT 'I would have a bike'). 'Be used to + noun/-ing' means you are accustomed to something now (I'm used to the noise; I'm used to working nights). 'Get used to + noun/-ing' means becoming accustomed (You'll get used to it). The classic Hindi-speaker error is 'I am used to wake up early', mixing the two patterns. After 'be/get used to', the 'to' is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.
concept_hi: ये एक जैसे दिखते हैं पर मतलब अलग है। 'Used to + क्रिया' अतीत की वह आदत या स्थिति जो अब नहीं है (I used to smoke)। 'Would + क्रिया' भी अतीत की दोहराई गई क्रिया है, पर सिर्फ़ क्रिया, स्थिति नहीं (We would play cricket every evening, पर 'I would have a bike' गलत)। 'Be used to + संज्ञा/-ing' का मतलब है कि आप अब किसी चीज़ के आदी हैं (I'm used to the noise; I'm used to working nights)। 'Get used to + संज्ञा/-ing' = आदी होना (You'll get used to it)। हिंदी भाषियों की क्लासिक गलती है 'I am used to wake up early'। 'be/get used to' के बाद 'to' preposition है, इसलिए क्रिया में -ing लगता है।
pattern: used to + V1 (past habit/state, not now) | didn't use to + V1 | would + V1 (past repeated ACTION) | be used to + noun / V-ing (accustomed now) | get used to + noun / V-ing (becoming accustomed)

title: Linking words and discourse markers
concept_en: Linking words show the relationship between ideas: contrast (however, whereas, although, despite), result (therefore, as a result, consequently), addition (moreover, furthermore, in addition), and example (for instance). Grammar matters: 'although/though/whereas/while' join two clauses; 'despite/in spite of' take a noun or -ing (never 'despite of'); 'however/therefore/moreover' are adverbs that start a new sentence or follow a semicolon, with a comma after them. 'But' joins clauses inside one sentence and does not usually start a formal sentence. Do not stack markers ('but however'). Choose one, place it correctly, and punctuate it.
concept_hi: Linking words विचारों के बीच संबंध दिखाते हैं: विरोध (however, whereas, although, despite), नतीजा (therefore, as a result, consequently), जोड़ (moreover, furthermore, in addition), उदाहरण (for instance)। व्याकरण महत्वपूर्ण है: 'although/though/whereas/while' दो clause जोड़ते हैं; 'despite/in spite of' के बाद संज्ञा या -ing आता है (कभी 'despite of' नहीं); 'however/therefore/moreover' क्रियाविशेषण हैं जो नए वाक्य की शुरुआत या semicolon के बाद आते हैं और उनके बाद कॉमा लगता है। 'but' एक ही वाक्य में clause जोड़ता है। मार्कर न जोड़ें ('but however')। एक चुनें, सही जगह रखें, सही विराम लगाएँ।
pattern: Although/Though/Whereas/While + clause, + clause | Despite/In spite of + noun/-ing, + clause | Clause. However/Therefore/Moreover, + clause | clause; however, clause | clause, but clause

examples.en: The exploit works on Linux, whereas the Windows build is unaffected.
examples.hi: एक्सप्लॉइट लिनक्स पर काम करता है, जबकि विंडोज़ बिल्ड प्रभावित नहीं है।

examples.en: The server was patched. However, the vulnerability was still exploitable.
examples.hi: सर्वर पैच किया गया था। फिर भी, खामी का फ़ायदा उठाया जा सकता था।

examples.en: The logs were deleted; therefore, we cannot confirm the timeline.
examples.hi: लॉग मिटा दिए गए थे; इसलिए, हम समयरेखा की पुष्टि नहीं कर सकते।

examples.en: The app stores passwords in plain text. Moreover, it sends them over HTTP.
examples.hi: ऐप पासवर्ड सादे टेक्स्ट में रखता है। इसके अलावा, उन्हें HTTP पर भेजता है।

examples.en: Several controls failed. For instance, MFA was disabled for admin accounts.
examples.hi: कई नियंत्रण विफल रहे। उदाहरण के लिए, एडमिन खातों पर MFA बंद था।

examples.en: The team was small but highly effective.
examples.hi: टीम छोटी थी लेकिन बहुत प्रभावी थी।

examples.en: As a result of the outage, the client lost two hours of sales.
examples.hi: आउटेज के परिणामस्वरूप, क्लाइंट की दो घंटे की बिक्री का नुकसान हुआ।

contrast.wrong: Despite of the rain, we went out.
contrast.right: Despite the rain, we went out. / In spite of the rain, we went out.
contrast.why_en: 'Despite' never takes 'of'. Learners blend it with 'in spite of'.
contrast.why_hi: 'despite' के बाद कभी 'of' नहीं आता। यह 'in spite of' से मिल जाता है।

contrast.wrong: Although it was late, but we continued.
contrast.right: Although it was late, we continued.
contrast.why_en: One contrast word is enough. Hindi 'हालाँकि … लेकिन' uses two, English uses one.
contrast.why_hi: एक विरोध शब्द काफ़ी है। हिंदी 'हालाँकि … लेकिन' में दो होते हैं, अंग्रेज़ी में एक।

contrast.wrong: The patch was applied, however the bug remained.
contrast.right: The patch was applied. However, the bug remained. / The patch was applied; however, the bug remained.
contrast.why_en: 'However' cannot join two clauses with only a comma (comma splice). Use a full stop or semicolon.
contrast.why_hi: 'however' सिर्फ़ कॉमा से दो clause नहीं जोड़ सकता (comma splice)। full stop या semicolon लगाएँ।

contrast.wrong: He is very experienced, therefore he got the job.
contrast.right: He is very experienced; therefore, he got the job. / He is very experienced, so he got the job.
contrast.why_en: 'Therefore' is an adverb, not a conjunction. Use 'so' for a comma join.
contrast.why_hi: 'therefore' क्रियाविशेषण है, conjunction नहीं। कॉमा से जोड़ना हो तो 'so' लगाएँ।

practice.prompt: Despite of the high severity, the ticket was ignored.
answer: Despite the high severity, the ticket was ignored.
In spite of the high severity, the ticket was ignored.
practice.hi: उच्च गंभीरता के बावजूद, टिकट को अनदेखा किया गया।
practice.feedback_hi: 'despite' के बाद 'of' नहीं।

practice.prompt: ___ the budget was cut, the project finished on time.
practice.hi: हालाँकि बजट कम कर दिया गया, प्रोजेक्ट समय पर पूरा हुआ।
practice.feedback_en: A full clause follows → 'Although'. 'Despite' needs a noun.
practice.feedback_hi: पूरा clause आ रहा है → 'Although'। 'Despite' के बाद संज्ञा चाहिए।

practice.prompt: The API is public. ___, it has no rate limiting.
practice.hi: API सार्वजनिक है। इसके अलावा, इसमें रेट लिमिटिंग नहीं है।
practice.feedback_hi: दूसरी समस्या जोड़ना → 'Moreover'।

practice.prompt: Although the code compiled, but the tests failed.
answer: Although the code compiled, the tests failed.
The code compiled, but the tests failed.
practice.hi: हालाँकि कोड कंपाइल हुआ, टेस्ट फेल हो गए।
practice.feedback_hi: 'although' या 'but', दोनों नहीं।

practice.prompt: Version 2 encrypts data at rest, ___ version 1 stored it in plain text.
practice.hi: संस्करण 2 डेटा को एन्क्रिप्ट करता है, जबकि संस्करण 1 उसे सादे टेक्स्ट में रखता था।
practice.feedback_hi: दो तथ्यों में विरोध → 'whereas' / 'while'।

practice.prompt: 'The exploit is public; therefore, we rate this as critical.' is correctly punctuated.
practice.hi: 'The exploit is public; therefore, we rate this as critical.' सही विराम-चिह्न वाला है?
practice.feedback_hi: सही: 'therefore' से पहले semicolon, बाद में कॉमा।

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
answer: In spite of the fix, the app still crashes.
practice.hi: सुधार के बावजूद, ऐप अब भी क्रैश होता है।
practice.feedback_hi: In spite of + संज्ञा, + clause।

practice.prompt: The backup failed, however nobody noticed for a week.
answer: The backup failed. However, nobody noticed for a week.
The backup failed; however, nobody noticed for a week.
practice.hi: बैकअप विफल हुआ। फिर भी, एक हफ़्ते तक किसी ने ध्यान नहीं दिया।
practice.feedback_en: 'However' needs a full stop or semicolon before it, comma after.
practice.feedback_hi: 'however' से पहले full stop या semicolon, बाद में कॉमा।

practice.prompt: Several endpoints lack authentication. ___, /admin/export returns all user records.
practice.hi: कई endpoint में प्रमाणीकरण नहीं है। उदाहरण के लिए, /admin/export सभी उपयोगकर्ता रिकॉर्ड लौटाता है।
practice.feedback_hi: उदाहरण देना → 'For instance'।

practice.prompt: The certificate expired; ___ a result, all API calls failed.
practice.hi: सर्टिफ़िकेट की अवधि समाप्त हो गई; परिणामस्वरूप, सभी API कॉल विफल हुए।
practice.feedback_hi: 'As a result' परिणाम दिखाता है।

production.task_en: Write a 3-sentence mini-summary of a bug or incident using: one 'although/despite' sentence, one 'However,' sentence, and one 'therefore/as a result' sentence.
production.task_hi: किसी बग या घटना का 3 वाक्यों का सारांश लिखें: एक 'although/despite' वाला, एक 'However,' वाला, और एक 'therefore/as a result' वाला वाक्य।

title: Causatives: have/get something done, make/let/get someone do
concept_en: Causative structures say that you arrange for someone else to do something. 'Have/get + object + past participle' means you did not do it yourself: 'I had my laptop repaired', 'We got the code reviewed'. 'Have + person + bare verb' (I had the intern update the docs) and 'get + person + to-verb' (I got the intern to update the docs) name who did it. 'Make + person + bare verb' means force (The manager made us rewrite it); 'let + person + bare verb' means allow (Let me check). 'Have something done' can also describe something bad that happened to you: 'She had her phone stolen'. Hindi speakers tend to write 'I repaired my laptop' when someone else did it, and to add 'to' after make and let.
concept_hi: Causative ढाँचे बताते हैं कि आपने किसी और से काम करवाया। 'have/get + वस्तु + तीसरा रूप' = आपने खुद नहीं किया: 'I had my laptop repaired', 'We got the code reviewed'। 'have + व्यक्ति + क्रिया का पहला रूप' (I had the intern update the docs) और 'get + व्यक्ति + to + क्रिया' (I got the intern to update the docs) बताते हैं कि किसने किया। 'make + व्यक्ति + क्रिया' = मजबूर करना; 'let + व्यक्ति + क्रिया' = अनुमति देना। 'have something done' किसी बुरी घटना के लिए भी: 'She had her phone stolen'। हिंदी भाषी अक्सर 'I repaired my laptop' लिख देते हैं जब किसी और ने किया हो, और make/let के बाद 'to' जोड़ देते हैं।
pattern: have/get + object + V3 (someone else does it) | have + person + V1 | get + person + to + V1 | make + person + V1 (force) | let + person + V1 (allow) | have + object + V3 (bad experience)

examples.en: I had my car serviced last week.
examples.hi: मैंने पिछले हफ़्ते अपनी कार की सर्विस करवाई।

examples.en: We got the pen-test report translated into Hindi.
examples.hi: हमने पेन-टेस्ट रिपोर्ट का हिंदी में अनुवाद करवाया।
examples.note: get + object + V3 (more informal than have).

examples.en: She had the vendor sign an NDA before the call.
examples.hi: उसने कॉल से पहले वेंडर से NDA पर हस्ताक्षर करवाए।

examples.en: I got my colleague to double-check the firewall rules.
examples.hi: मैंने अपने सहकर्मी से फ़ायरवॉल नियमों की दोबारा जाँच करवाई।

examples.en: The auditor made us re-run every test.
examples.hi: ऑडिटर ने हमें हर टेस्ट दोबारा चलाने पर मजबूर किया।

examples.en: Let me know if the build fails.
examples.hi: अगर बिल्ड फेल हो तो मुझे बताना।

examples.en: He had his wallet stolen on the train.
examples.hi: ट्रेन में उसका बटुआ चोरी हो गया।

examples.en: You should get your eyes tested.
examples.hi: तुम्हें अपनी आँखों की जाँच करवानी चाहिए।

examples.en: The company is having a new office built in Gandhinagar.
examples.hi: कंपनी गांधीनगर में नया ऑफ़िस बनवा रही है।

examples.en: They won't let us access production without a ticket.
examples.hi: वे हमें बिना टिकट के प्रोडक्शन तक पहुँचने नहीं देंगे।

contrast.wrong: I cut my hair yesterday.
contrast.right: I had my hair cut yesterday.
contrast.why_en: Unless you cut it yourself, use the causative. Hindi 'बाल कटवाए' has a special causative verb form; English needs have/get + V3.
contrast.why_hi: अगर आपने खुद नहीं काटे, causative लगाएँ। हिंदी 'कटवाए' में प्रेरणार्थक रूप है; अंग्रेज़ी में have/get + तीसरा रूप चाहिए।

contrast.wrong: The manager made us to work late.
contrast.right: The manager made us work late.
contrast.why_en: 'Make' takes the bare infinitive, no 'to'.
contrast.why_hi: 'make' के बाद 'to' नहीं आता।

contrast.wrong: Please let me to explain.
contrast.right: Please let me explain.
contrast.why_en: 'Let' also takes the bare infinitive.
contrast.why_hi: 'let' के बाद भी 'to' नहीं आता।

contrast.wrong: I got the team review the design.
contrast.right: I got the team to review the design. / I had the team review the design.
contrast.why_en: 'Get + person' needs 'to'; 'have + person' does not.
contrast.why_hi: 'get + व्यक्ति' के साथ 'to' चाहिए; 'have + व्यक्ति' के साथ नहीं।

practice.prompt: We ___ (have / the logs / analyse) by an external firm.
practice.hi: हमने लॉग का विश्लेषण एक बाहरी फर्म से करवाया।
practice.feedback_hi: have + वस्तु + तीसरा रूप।

practice.prompt: The teacher made the students to rewrite the essay.
answer: The teacher made the students rewrite the essay.
practice.hi: शिक्षक ने छात्रों से निबंध दोबारा लिखवाया।
practice.feedback_hi: make + व्यक्ति + क्रिया, 'to' नहीं।

practice.prompt: I ___ the intern ___ the dependency list.
practice.hi: मैंने इंटर्न से डिपेंडेंसी सूची अपडेट करवाई।
practice.feedback_hi: get + व्यक्ति + to + क्रिया।

practice.prompt: I painted my house last month by a contractor.
answer: I had my house painted last month by a contractor.
I had my house painted by a contractor last month.
practice.hi: मैंने पिछले महीने एक ठेकेदार से घर की पुताई करवाई।
practice.feedback_en: Someone else did it → had + object + V3.
practice.feedback_hi: किसी और ने किया → had + वस्तु + तीसरा रूप।

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
answer: Please let the team know the outcome.
practice.hi: कृपया टीम को नतीजा बता दें।
practice.feedback_hi: let + व्यक्ति + क्रिया।

practice.prompt: 'She had her account hacked' means she arranged for it to be hacked.
practice.hi: 'She had her account hacked' का मतलब है कि उसने खुद हैक करवाया?
practice.feedback_en: False. Here 'have + object + V3' describes a bad thing that happened to her.
practice.feedback_hi: गलत। यहाँ 'have + वस्तु + तीसरा रूप' उसके साथ हुई बुरी घटना बताता है।

practice.prompt: You should ___ (get / that mole / check) by a doctor.
practice.hi: तुम्हें उस तिल की डॉक्टर से जाँच करवानी चाहिए।
practice.feedback_hi: get + वस्तु + तीसरा रूप।

practice.prompt: The CISO ___ every engineer complete the phishing training.
practice.hi: CISO ने हर इंजीनियर से फ़िशिंग प्रशिक्षण पूरा करवाया।
practice.feedback_en: have + person + V1 ('complete'). 'Got' would need 'to complete'.
practice.feedback_hi: have + व्यक्ति + क्रिया ('complete')। 'got' के साथ 'to complete' चाहिए होता।

practice.prompt: They don't let us to install software ourselves.
answer: They don't let us install software ourselves.
practice.hi: वे हमें खुद सॉफ़्टवेयर इंस्टॉल करने नहीं देते।
practice.feedback_hi: let + व्यक्ति + क्रिया।

practice.prompt: We are ___ a new access policy ___ by legal.
practice.hi: हम कानूनी टीम से नई एक्सेस नीति का मसौदा बनवा रहे हैं।
practice.feedback_en: Continuous causative: are having + object + V3.
practice.feedback_hi: Continuous causative: are having + वस्तु + तीसरा रूप।

production.task_en: Write 3 sentences: something you had done recently (have + object + V3), something someone made you do, and something you got a colleague to do.
production.task_hi: 3 वाक्य लिखें: कुछ जो आपने हाल में करवाया (have + वस्तु + तीसरा रूप), कुछ जो किसी ने आपसे ज़बरदस्ती करवाया, और कुछ जो आपने किसी सहकर्मी से करवाया।

title: Inversion and emphasis
concept_en: When a negative or limiting adverbial starts a sentence, the subject and auxiliary swap places, exactly like a question: 'Not only did the patch fail, it also corrupted data', 'Seldom have I seen such a clean codebase', 'Only then did we realise the scope'. If there is no auxiliary, add do/does/did. Common triggers: not only, never, rarely, seldom, hardly … when, no sooner … than, only after/when/then, under no circumstances, at no time, little. 'So + adjective' and 'such + noun' can also front for emphasis: 'So severe was the bug that we halted the release'. Use this in formal writing and speeches; in casual chat it sounds dramatic.
concept_hi: जब वाक्य की शुरुआत नकारात्मक या सीमित करने वाले क्रियाविशेषण से होती है, तो कर्ता और सहायक क्रिया की जगह बदल जाती है, बिल्कुल सवाल की तरह: 'Not only did the patch fail, it also corrupted data', 'Seldom have I seen such a clean codebase', 'Only then did we realise the scope'। सहायक क्रिया न हो तो do/does/did जोड़ें। आम ट्रिगर: not only, never, rarely, seldom, hardly … when, no sooner … than, only after/when/then, under no circumstances, at no time, little। 'So + विशेषण' और 'such + संज्ञा' भी ज़ोर के लिए आगे आ सकते हैं। यह औपचारिक लेखन और भाषण में चलता है; रोज़मर्रा की बातचीत में नाटकीय लगता है।
pattern: Negative/limiting adverbial + auxiliary + subject + verb | Not only + aux + S + V, but (also)… | Hardly + had + S + V3 when… | No sooner + had + S + V3 than… | Only after/when + clause + aux + S + V | So + adj + aux + S that… | Such + be + noun that…

examples.en: Not only did the attacker steal data, but they also deleted the backups.
examples.hi: हमलावर ने न केवल डेटा चुराया, बल्कि बैकअप भी मिटा दिए।

examples.en: Never have I seen a report written so clearly.
examples.hi: मैंने कभी इतनी स्पष्ट लिखी रिपोर्ट नहीं देखी।

examples.en: Rarely does a critical bug get fixed within an hour.
examples.hi: शायद ही कभी कोई गंभीर बग एक घंटे में ठीक होता है।

examples.en: Hardly had we restored the service when it crashed again.
examples.hi: हमने सेवा बहाल ही की थी कि वह फिर क्रैश हो गई।

examples.en: No sooner had I sent the email than I noticed the typo.
examples.hi: मैंने ईमेल भेजा ही था कि मुझे टाइपो दिखा।

examples.en: Only after the second audit did management take the risk seriously.
examples.hi: दूसरे ऑडिट के बाद ही प्रबंधन ने जोखिम को गंभीरता से लिया।
examples.note: Inversion in the main clause, not the 'after' clause.

examples.en: Under no circumstances should credentials be shared over chat.
examples.hi: किसी भी हालत में क्रेडेंशियल चैट पर साझा नहीं किए जाने चाहिए।

examples.en: So slow was the old system that nobody used it.
examples.hi: पुराना सिस्टम इतना धीमा था कि कोई उसे इस्तेमाल नहीं करता था।

examples.en: Little did we know that the vendor had already been breached.
examples.hi: हमें ज़रा भी पता नहीं था कि वेंडर पर पहले ही सेंध लग चुकी है।

examples.en: Such was the impact that the CEO issued a public apology.
examples.hi: असर इतना बड़ा था कि सीईओ ने सार्वजनिक माफ़ी माँगी।

contrast.wrong: Not only the patch failed, but it also corrupted data.
contrast.right: Not only did the patch fail, but it also corrupted data.
contrast.why_en: After 'Not only' at the start, you must invert with did/does/do. Hindi 'न केवल' needs no change in word order.
contrast.why_hi: शुरुआत में 'Not only' हो तो did/does/do के साथ उलटना ज़रूरी है। हिंदी 'न केवल' में क्रम नहीं बदलता।

contrast.wrong: Never I have seen such traffic.
contrast.right: Never have I seen such traffic.
contrast.why_en: The auxiliary must come before the subject.
contrast.why_hi: सहायक क्रिया कर्ता से पहले आएगी।

contrast.wrong: Only after we checked the logs, we found the cause.
contrast.right: Only after we checked the logs did we find the cause.
contrast.why_en: With 'only after + clause', the inversion happens in the main clause.
contrast.why_hi: 'only after + clause' में उलटाव मुख्य clause में होता है।

contrast.wrong: Hardly we had started when the alarm rang.
contrast.right: Hardly had we started when the alarm rang.
contrast.why_en: 'Hardly' takes past perfect with inversion: had + subject.
contrast.why_hi: 'hardly' के साथ past perfect और उलटाव: had + कर्ता।

practice.prompt: Not only he ignored the alert, he also disabled it.
answer: Not only did he ignore the alert, he also disabled it.
Not only did he ignore the alert, but he also disabled it.
practice.hi: उसने न केवल अलर्ट को अनदेखा किया, बल्कि उसे बंद भी कर दिया।
practice.feedback_hi: Not only + did + कर्ता + क्रिया।

practice.prompt: Seldom ___ such a detailed write-up.
practice.hi: हमें शायद ही कभी इतना विस्तृत विवरण मिलता है।
practice.feedback_hi: Seldom + do + कर्ता + क्रिया।

title: Past modals: should have, must have, might have, needn't have, could have
concept_en: Modal + have + past participle looks back at the past. 'Should have / ought to have' = it was the right thing but did not happen (regret or criticism). 'Must have' = I am almost certain it happened; 'can't have / couldn't have' = I am almost certain it did not. 'May/might/could have' = it was possible. 'Could have' also means ability not used ('I could have called'). 'Needn't have + V3' = you did it but it was unnecessary; 'didn't need to' = it was unnecessary, and usually you did not do it. 'Would have' = an imagined past result. Hindi has one word 'चाहिए था' for should have and 'होगा' for must have, so keep the English forms separate.
concept_hi: Modal + have + तीसरा रूप अतीत की ओर देखता है। 'should have / ought to have' = यह सही था पर हुआ नहीं (पछतावा या आलोचना)। 'must have' = मुझे लगभग यकीन है कि हुआ; 'can't have / couldn't have' = लगभग यकीन है कि नहीं हुआ। 'may/might/could have' = संभव था। 'could have' का मतलब इस्तेमाल न की गई क्षमता भी ('I could have called')। 'needn't have + तीसरा रूप' = आपने किया पर ज़रूरत नहीं थी; 'didn't need to' = ज़रूरत नहीं थी, और आमतौर पर किया भी नहीं। 'would have' = अतीत का काल्पनिक नतीजा। हिंदी में 'चाहिए था' और 'होगा' एक-एक शब्द हैं, इसलिए अंग्रेज़ी रूपों को अलग रखें।
pattern: should/ought to + have + V3 (right thing, not done) | must have + V3 (near-certain yes) | can't/couldn't have + V3 (near-certain no) | may/might/could have + V3 (possible) | needn't have + V3 (done, unnecessary) | didn't need to + V1 (unnecessary, probably not done)

title: Participle clauses
concept_en: Participle clauses shorten sentences in formal writing. A present participle (-ing) replaces an active clause with the same subject: 'Knowing the risk, we disabled the feature' (= Because we knew…). A past participle (V3) replaces a passive: 'Written in Rust, the tool is memory-safe' (= Because it is written…). 'Having + V3' shows one action finished before another: 'Having patched the server, we re-ran the scan'. The golden rule: the subject of the participle must be the subject of the main clause. 'Walking into the room, the alarm went off' wrongly says the alarm was walking (a dangling participle). Participle clauses also follow nouns to replace relative clauses: 'the engineer leading the audit', 'the data stored on the device'.
concept_hi: Participle clause औपचारिक लेखन में वाक्य छोटा करते हैं। Present participle (-ing) उसी कर्ता वाले active clause की जगह लेता है: 'Knowing the risk, we disabled the feature' (= क्योंकि हमें पता था…)। Past participle (तीसरा रूप) passive की जगह: 'Written in Rust, the tool is memory-safe'। 'Having + तीसरा रूप' दिखाता है कि एक क्रिया दूसरी से पहले पूरी हुई: 'Having patched the server, we re-ran the scan'। सुनहरा नियम: participle का कर्ता और मुख्य clause का कर्ता एक ही होना चाहिए। 'Walking into the room, the alarm went off' गलत है क्योंकि इसमें अलार्म चल रहा है (dangling participle)। Participle clause संज्ञा के बाद relative clause की जगह भी आते हैं: 'the engineer leading the audit', 'the data stored on the device'।
pattern: V-ing + clause, main clause (same subject, active) | V3 + clause, main clause (passive) | Having + V3 …, main clause (earlier action) | Not + V-ing … | noun + V-ing / V3 (reduced relative clause) | After/Before/While/When + V-ing

examples.en: Realising the token had leaked, we revoked it immediately.
examples.hi: यह समझते ही कि टोकन लीक हो गया है, हमने उसे तुरंत रद्द कर दिया।

examples.en: Built on an outdated framework, the portal was easy to exploit.
examples.hi: पुराने फ़्रेमवर्क पर बना होने के कारण, पोर्टल को आसानी से एक्सप्लॉइट किया जा सकता था।

examples.en: Having reviewed the logs, the analyst confirmed the intrusion.
examples.hi: लॉग की समीक्षा करने के बाद, विश्लेषक ने घुसपैठ की पुष्टि की।

examples.en: Not wanting to alarm users, the company delayed the announcement.
examples.hi: उपयोगकर्ताओं को घबराना नहीं चाहते हुए, कंपनी ने घोषणा में देरी की।

examples.en: The engineer leading the migration has ten years' experience.
examples.hi: माइग्रेशन का नेतृत्व कर रहे इंजीनियर के पास दस साल का अनुभव है।

examples.en: All data stored on the device is encrypted.
examples.hi: डिवाइस पर संग्रहीत सारा डेटा एन्क्रिप्टेड है।

examples.en: After finishing the scan, export the results as CSV.
examples.hi: स्कैन पूरा करने के बाद, नतीजे CSV में निर्यात करें।

examples.en: While testing the API, she discovered an unauthenticated endpoint.
examples.hi: API टेस्ट करते समय, उसे बिना प्रमाणीकरण वाला endpoint मिला।

examples.en: Having been warned twice, he was finally suspended.
examples.hi: दो बार चेतावनी मिलने के बाद, उसे आखिरकार निलंबित कर दिया गया।

examples.en: The report, written in haste, contained several errors.
examples.hi: जल्दबाज़ी में लिखी गई रिपोर्ट में कई गलतियाँ थीं।
examples.note: Participle between commas after a noun.

contrast.wrong: Walking into the server room, the temperature was shocking.
contrast.right: Walking into the server room, I was shocked by the temperature.
contrast.why_en: The temperature was not walking. The participle's subject must be the main subject. Hindi 'कमरे में जाते ही तापमान…' allows this; English does not.
contrast.why_hi: तापमान चल नहीं रहा था। participle का कर्ता मुख्य कर्ता होना चाहिए। हिंदी 'जाते ही तापमान…' में यह चलता है; अंग्रेज़ी में नहीं।

contrast.wrong: Finished the report, she sent it to the client.
contrast.right: Having finished the report, she sent it to the client.
contrast.why_en: She did the finishing (active, earlier), so 'Having finished'. A bare past participle means passive.
contrast.why_hi: उसने खत्म किया (active, पहले), इसलिए 'Having finished'। अकेला तीसरा रूप passive होता है।

contrast.wrong: The bug reporting by the researcher was critical.
contrast.right: The bug reported by the researcher was critical.
contrast.why_en: The bug was reported (passive) → past participle.
contrast.why_hi: बग रिपोर्ट किया गया (passive) → तीसरा रूप।

contrast.wrong: Being tired, so I went home early.
contrast.right: Being tired, I went home early.
contrast.why_en: The participle clause already gives the reason; do not add 'so'.
contrast.why_hi: participle clause पहले से कारण दे रहा है; 'so' न जोड़ें।

practice.prompt: ___ (know) the deadline was close, we skipped the optional tests.
practice.hi: डेडलाइन करीब जानकर, हमने वैकल्पिक टेस्ट छोड़ दिए।
practice.feedback_hi: Active, वही कर्ता → Knowing।

practice.prompt: ___ (write) by an intern, the script had no error handling.

practice.feedback_hi: Passive → तीसरा रूप 'Written'।

answer: Reading the email, I thought the attachment looked suspicious.

practice.feedback_en: Dangling participle: the attachment was not reading. Make the reader the subject.
practice.feedback_hi: Dangling participle: अटैचमेंट पढ़ नहीं रहा था। पढ़ने वाले को कर्ता बनाएँ।

practice.prompt: ___ the vulnerability, the team notified the vendor.
practice.hi: खामी की पुष्टि करने के बाद, टीम ने वेंडर को सूचित किया।

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
answer: All data stored on the device is encrypted.

practice.feedback_en: Reduced relative clause: data (that is) stored…
practice.feedback_hi: छोटा relative clause: data (that is) stored…

practice.feedback_en: True: Not + having + V3 for a negative earlier action.
practice.feedback_hi: सही: नकारात्मक पहले की क्रिया के लिए Not + having + तीसरा रूप।

practice.prompt: The person responsibling for backups is on leave.

practice.feedback_hi: 'responsible' विशेषण है, क्रिया नहीं; participle नहीं चाहिए।
